content: I remember reading discussion about this, but I cannot find it on Zulip. Can someone help me find it?
The title reminds me of #graph theory > (Undirected) hypergraphs @ 💬 but idk if that's what you meant
In the definition of docs#Graph, there's vertexSet and edgeSet. I think the other idea was to not have them, in other words basically assume that vertexSet/edgeSet are Set.univ.
Oh, maybe I should just look at the commit history for docs#Graph.

Ah, yes, I found it.
#graph theory > What kind of graphs are in Mathlib already?
#PR reviews > #24122 Multigraphs
btw in case you missed it: https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/31120#issuecomment-3562965722
I guess this means refactoring SimpleGraph to use a Set

Snir Broshi said:

I guess this means refactoring SimpleGraph to use a Set

Well, this already exists as docs#Graph and docs#SimpleGraph.Subgraph.
@Yaël Dillies @Bhavik Mehta, do you mind elaborating on the github comment linked above?
The idea would be to switch to the sort of SimpleGraph definition @Alex Kontorovich wrote in google-deepmind/formal-conjectures#296, and then subgraphs can have the same type as graphs
Essentially the definition that we'd discussed privately in the past, Peter!

This doesn't solve the problem of contractions though, right? You could go even further and have an equivalence relation on V as well, with two terms of type V equivalent meaning "these are the same vertex" and adjacency behaving well wrt this equivalence relation. Then you can contract, delete and add edges to your heart's content.

We've experimented with that, Kevin, and it seems to be a pain. You have this explicit equivalence relation that needs to carry forward to structure definitions such as walks/paths, and you have to pay enough attention to the equivalence relation explicitly that it becomes a large cognitive load. As I expressed in the other topic, I am leaning more towards the idea the 'retraction' point of view is best for minors.

Yes, I remember messing around with this a while ago. My various attempts at quotienting the vertex set led to subtype hell, and it came out much nicer to just track the equivalence relation explicitly, without changing the underlying types... I think my latest attempt was here: #maths > Graph Minors @ 💬 which was already a while ago... Has there been any progress since then?
Oh this vertex set thing? I recall offering to make the PR six months ago on discord but @Bhavik Mehta said it wasn’t likely to get a timely review at that time.
I wanted it partly because we were working on Berge’s lemma and it was frustrating to coerce subgraphs to SimpleGraph.

Yaël Dillies said:

The idea would be to switch to the sort of SimpleGraph definition Alex Kontorovich wrote in google-deepmind/formal-conjectures#296, and then subgraphs can have the same type as graphs

Sounds good, btw do you think there's a good way to incorporate #4127 into this? (a HasAdj typeclass + instances for Digraph and SimpleGraph)
Also do you have a timeline in mind? Or are you looking for people to take this on? (no pressure)
Right now, all my refactoring energy is spent on monoid algebras in #25273. You should feel free to take this refactor on.
The HasAdj design is not fleshed out enough that we can use it, and IMO it is more or less orthogonal to making simple graphs supported on a set. Therefore I'd say "don't worry about it"
What's the status of this potential refactor, did anyone (start to) take it on?
I have a pr to offer for adoption #33466 that was passing CI as of yesterday
The review comments need to be addressed and the proofs and instances golfed
This adds vertex sets to Digraph.

I picked up @Shreyas Srinivas's vertex set Digraph refactor and was looking at doing the same for SimpleGraph but there are so many theorems and definitions that would be similar/identical between the two (e.g. IsSpanningSubgraph, DistribLattice instance, etc). I think the HasAdj typeclass is too general for this stuff but I'm wondering where we could move it if not there (GraphLike#36743 maybe?). I remember one idea was to define simple graphs with respect to digraphs by quotienting over edge orientation but that's not something we're considering anymore, is it?

Great! I think for SimpleGraph we should use GraphLike and then generalize theorems incrementally, rather than add vertex sets all at once which will probably be a huge PR. I also like that we could all collectively participate in such an effort.

As for relating Digraph and SimpleGraph with quotients (docs#Antisymmetrization ?), I think docs#Digraph.toSimpleGraphInclusive / docs#Digraph.toSimpleGraphStrict are great and quotients would make life harder.

Snir Broshi said:

Great! I think for SimpleGraph we should use GraphLike and then generalize theorems incrementally, rather than add vertex sets all at once which will probably be a huge PR. I also like that we could all collectively participate in such an effort.

Right, but what I'm asking is whether people think GraphLike could be an appropriate place to generalize the definitions and theorems that SimpleGraph currently has in common with Digraph. Sorry, this might not be the right channel for the discussion, I realized that this is actually something that should happen in parallel with the vertex set refactor stuff and I can move my message somewhere else.

At a very cursory glance it seems like HasAdj isn't a good place to generalize common definitions like the two I mentioned (IsSpanningSubgraph, DistribLattice instance), and GraphLike seems more appropriate, but I know the intention is mainly for generalizing walks. @Jun Kwon sorry for my ignorance, but is this something you intend for GraphLike? I'm not as familiar with defining graphs in terms of darts but it doesn't seem like that's the best context for talking about things like subgraphs, but another intermediary definition might also be strange

Hi, first of all, I would like to say that the definition of GraphLike is not quite set in stone as Graph with loop edges allows doesn't seem to allow a dart structure to be derived. The PR currently has a modification of the definition to allow Graph to bring a custom dart structure to instantiate GraphLike for each graph, but I am not 100% sure if it is the right solution.

If I were to put that problem aside and consider the previous definition of GraphLike, it is very much possible to capture the notion of subgraph: vertex set is a subset, dart set is subset and each dart is between the same pair of vertices. Spanning subgraph is just one more condition of vertex set being equal.

DistribLattice is a bit different as, similar to Graph, there is a compatibility issue: if two graphs, G1 and G2, where the dart with label d refers to a dart between u and v in G1 whereas it is a dart to x and y in G2. There is no obvious union of those two graphs. This is a limitation of each dart label not inherently tied to a pair of vertices.
Actually, for DistribLattice, if you were to restrict to a subgraph type, you still have CompletelyDistribLattice instance.
TLDR: Things get a bit messy with Graph but when it comes to Digraph and SimpleGraph, I am not wondering what I can generalize to GraphLike, I am wondering what GraphLike can't.

Jun Kwon said:

TLDR: Things get a bit messy with Graph but when it comes to Digraph and SimpleGraph, I am not wondering what I can generalize to GraphLike, I am wondering what GraphLike can't.

Ah makes sense, I was under the impression that GraphLike was more set in stone than it is
What's the source of the incompatibility with loop edges, out of curiosity?

Well, fundamentally it is simple: say e is a loop on v. We need two darts for each edge but there is no way to derive two different darts out of e without extra input or noncomputably choosing to create one out of thin air. The first one is our current solution (bring your own dart structure). Calling on axiom of choice leads to incompatibility with related graphs. (I talked about quite in detail in "Darts for Graph" channel. Perhaps, around this message in particular)

I spent sometime thinking about using GraphLike beyond just walks. At the moment, GraphLike is unaware of which pair constitutes an edge, and in the context of Graph, this make it impossible to define the right subgraph notion.
One thing that can be done is to extend GraphLike to be aware of edges. This makes it quite close to a definition of hypergraph. I would be happy to hear what people think about this change.
Lastly, the definition of GraphLike that include edges that I currently have in mind generalizes hypergraph and directed multigraph but Not directed hypergraph. I am not sure if there is a definition that generalizes undirected hypergraph and directed hypergraph and not sure how much of a loss to not support directed hypergraph.
